capabilityIntro: Drafting production for contractors, facilities teams and design consultants. Start with one to three representative sheets so your reviewer can check the CAD format, plotted output and review process.
buyerRoles: Utility and civil contractor project managers
Design and bid teams coordinating drawing revisions

capabilities.title: Utility and mechanical record drawings
capabilities.summary: Use approved field markups to revise a utility or mechanical set and track details that need field confirmation.
inputs: Approved field markups with revision and sheet references
Editable base CAD and dependent references
Target sheet list, plot standards and handoff deadline
outputs: Revised native CAD and plotted sheet set in the agreed format
Exception log with sheet references and reviewer actions
checks: Compare incorporated changes with the approved markups
Validate affected layers, external references and plot readability
Keep unresolved dimensions and tie-ins visible for the buyer’s decision

capabilities.title: Legacy PDF and raster conversion
capabilities.summary: Rebuild legible archive drawings as editable linework organized by the buyer’s layer and block standards.
inputs: Readable scan or PDF and a known dimension reference
Required file version, layer naming and drawing conventions
Instructions for gaps, blurry symbols and conflicting dimensions
outputs: Visual overlay or plotted source comparison
checks: Calibrate against the supplied dimension and cross-check another known interval when available
Review line alignment, labels and units against the source

capabilities.title: Civil and survey drafting production
capabilities.summary: Prepare plans, profiles and crossing exhibits from approved survey records, stationing and design instructions.
inputs: Reviewer-approved source data and point or feature codes
Horizontal reference, vertical datum and units
Sheet template, callout list and drafting instructions
outputs: Assigned AutoCAD or Civil 3D files in the agreed format
Plotted sheets and dependent file manifest
Source point and missing-data notes for assigned review
checks: Confirm source identifiers, units and coordinate handling
Reconcile profile station and elevation labels with approved inputs
Log unknown attributes and wait for reviewer direction where needed

capabilities.title: Building existing-conditions drafting
capabilities.summary: Turn field sketches and recorded measurements into an editable architectural base for the design team.
inputs: Dimensioned field sketch or authorized measured records
Room and opening notes with any areas flagged for verification
CAD template, unit convention and required layout list
outputs: Layered existing floor plan and supporting opening details
Plotted sheets with matching layout IDs and revisions
Opening or field verification register with source references
checks: Check tagged features and recorded opening widths against the source
Compare the CAD and plotted room dimensions and door symbols
Keep unverified conditions visible and route them to the client reviewer

capabilities.title: Addenda and drawing revisions
capabilities.summary: Carry supplied changes across affected sheets, then document the issue and the remaining inputs.
inputs: Batch priorities, reviewers and revision cadence
outputs: Each dated production batch with revision status
Manifest for files, references and unresolved inputs
Batch closeout notes for the designated reviewer
checks: Compare each revised sheet with its approved instruction
Confirm working files and plotted sheets match the issue register
Capture approved revision requests and return open decisions to the owner

formats: DWG or Civil 3D version agreed for production work
Plotted PDFs with matching sheet IDs and revisions
Drawing index, change log and agreed reference files
Editable DXF for the downloadable website samples
requirements: Authorized source set with revision and sheet references
Target CAD version, units, drawing template and plot conventions
Reference files, designated reviewer and secure transfer method
boundaries: The buyer’s accountable reviewer handles field verification, survey determinations and interpretation of design intent.
Engineering approval, professional sealing and permitting remain with the designated accountable professionals.
An unclear source detail stays logged until the buyer directs its disposition.

projects.title: Utility trench closeout
projects.summary: One approved field offset carried into a three-sheet record set, with a pending tie-in assigned for review.
projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side utility field markup and revised record plan

comparison.label: Before · Field markup
comparison.alt: Source plan with a dashed marked-up 14-foot offset and a circled tie-in
comparison.caption: M-01 supplies the offset and station limits. M-02 asks for a tie-in dimension at 1+80.

comparison.label: After · Record plan
comparison.alt: Revised solid green route with the original alignment in gray and open issue E-01 at the right
comparison.caption: The approved offset is in the editable record geometry. E-01 stays open across the plan, detail and change register.

projects.context: A simulated closeout lead supplies a marked-up utility alignment and illustrative conduit elevations. The handoff includes the record plan, supplied profile and tie-in detail, with the original markup available for comparison.
constraints: Use feet in a fictional local grid. Stations follow the original baseline.
Incorporate the approved 14-foot shift between 0+60 and 1+20. Retain supplied profile elevations.
Keep the tie-in dimension at 1+80 open for the designated reviewer.

approach.title: Separate approved work from review items
approach.text: Carry approved markup M-01 into the record geometry. Tie M-02 to E-01 in the register and on the detail.

approach.title: Update the record geometry
approach.text: Move the route between the station limits, keep the original line on its own layer and retain the supplied conduit profile.

approach.title: Prepare the issue package
approach.text: Assemble UT-01, UT-02 and UT-03 as named CAD layouts and matching 11 × 17-inch PDF sheets, then index each sheet by its source and review status.

deliverables: Layered DXF with UT-01 record plan, UT-02 profile and UT-03 tie-in detail
Matching vector PDF set and the source markup PDF
Sheet index and a source-linked change register with the open issue
verification: Check the modeled 14-foot offset between 0+60 and 1+20.
Open the three named layouts and compare sheet IDs and revisions to the PDF set.
Trace E-01 at 1+80 back to M-02 and verify who owes the next decision.
projects.review: The draft demonstrates a review issue. For a live package, the designated reviewer supplies the tie-in dimension and approves the final record. The example uses fictional coordinates and elevations.

projects.title: Legacy PDF to editable CAD
projects.summary: A raster utility-room plan redrawn as layered CAD, with two scale checks and one unreadable equipment tag logged.
projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side archive scan and editable CAD redraw of a utility room

comparison.label: Before · PDF scan
comparison.alt: Sepia raster scan of a utility room with 48-foot and 32-foot dimension references
comparison.caption: The archive scan provides two readable dimension references. The equipment tag near the return run is indistinct.

comparison.label: After · Layered CAD
comparison.alt: Clean CAD redraw with wall outlines, visible utility lines and a red L-01 review callout
comparison.caption: Editable walls, door, equipment footprints and visible pipe runs, with the source-tag exception identified as L-01.

projects.context: A fictional facilities manager supplies a scanned utility-room PDF. The redraw uses the 48-foot room width for scale, the independent 32-foot depth for a perpendicular check and the visible equipment and piping for linework.
constraints: Use the 48-foot horizontal dimension to calibrate the redraw.
Use the separately labeled 32-foot vertical dimension to check scale in the other axis.
Retain the blurry tag location and log the missing identifier as L-01.

approach.title: Calibrate the source
approach.text: Match the known room width to 48 drawing units. Compare the perpendicular wall extent against the independent 32-foot dimension.

approach.title: Organize editable lines
approach.text: Separate the room bounds, door, visible piping and equipment footprints into named layers. Carry the unclear tag as a review callout.

approach.title: Record conversion rules
approach.text: Plot LEG-01 from the same geometry, then map each feature to its target layer and log the source issue for the records owner.

deliverables: LEG-01 layered DXF with one named drawing layout
Matching vector redraw PDF and original synthetic raster PDF
Source-to-layer crosswalk with open issue L-01
verification: Measure the editable room envelope at 48 by 32 feet in model space.
Compare the door, equipment and pipes in the source scan with the plotted redraw.
Find L-01 in the CAD layout and crosswalk, then identify the records owner’s next action.
projects.review: The draft demonstrates translation from a synthetic scan. On a live job, the records owner confirms the equipment tag and the approved source before release.

projects.title: Commercial service court grading package
projects.summary: A 120-foot curb-line profile carries the approved grading markup while preserving both end elevations.

handoffSummary.Source: Five survey stations and a prime consultant’s markup
handoffSummary.Drawing set: CV-01 grading plan and CV-02 profile
handoffSummary.Open review: Survey elevation at the east connection

projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side source and finished drawing for commercial service court grading package

comparison.label: Before · Supplied field data
comparison.alt: Existing curb and five labeled survey elevations across a service court
comparison.caption: CV-M1 records the existing curb, inlet and elevation references used by the prime.

comparison.label: After · Grading markup
comparison.alt: A revised green grading line on the original curb base with an east connection callout
comparison.caption: The revised line uses the supplied markup. The east connection stays open.

projects.context: A fictional civil consultant needs an existing base and an approved grading markup assembled for review. The plan and profile share the five supplied survey stations.
constraints: Use the supplied local vertical datum and work in feet.
Hold the surveyed end matches at 100.20 and 99.55 feet.
Carry the proposed elevations as supplied and retain the existing profile as a reference.

approach.title: Check the source stations
approach.text: Tie the five records to CV-M1 and compare the 0+00 and 1+20 match points.

approach.title: Draft the plan and profile
approach.text: Keep existing and revised linework on separate layers. Use the source elevations to plot the profile.

approach.title: Track the missing spot elevation
approach.text: Key the east connection on CV-01 and assign the follow-up to the prime’s survey reviewer.

deliverables: CV-01 site plan and CV-02 curb-line profile in editable CAD and matching PDFs
Supplied elevations in CSV and a source sheet for comparison
Review register for the open connection
verification: Check the horizontal station span from 0+00 to 1+20.
At 0+60, reconcile existing 99.95 feet and revised 99.90 feet against the source CSV.
Verify both shared end elevations and the east connection callout before release.
projects.review: The prime retains grading decisions. Its survey reviewer confirms the missing east connection elevation.

handoffSummary.Drawing set: TI-01 existing plan and TI-02 opening detail

projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side source and finished drawing for tenant suite existing-conditions drawings

comparison.label: Before · Field sketch
comparison.alt: Three-room shell and field note for opening D-02
comparison.caption: The source measures the shell and records the opening locations and widths.

comparison.label: After · Editable floor plan
comparison.alt: Existing suite with room labels, two door swings and tag D-02
comparison.caption: The floor plan shows the measured partitions and door swings. D-02 stays tagged for the height check.

projects.context: A fictional tenant improvement team supplies field notes for a three-room suite. The architect needs an editable existing base and a record of the incomplete opening measurement.
constraints: Use the field sketch’s shell dimensions and measured partition locations.
Draw D-01 and D-02 from the supplied opening notes.
Carry D-02’s width and keep the missing head height open.

approach.title: Build the base plan
approach.text: Draft the 48-by-34-foot shell and existing partitions in feet.

approach.title: Connect the drawing tags
approach.text: Use D-01 and D-02 on TI-01 and check the D-02 detail on TI-02.

approach.title: Log the field check
approach.text: Record supplied widths and the head-height question in the opening register.

deliverables: Editable floor plan and opening detail layouts
Matching two-sheet PDF and field-sketch PDF
Opening register with source references
verification: Check the 48-by-34-foot shell against TI-M1.
Measure the four-foot D-02 opening in the plan and detail.
Trace D-02 to the register and confirm the head height remains open.
projects.review: The client’s field reviewer verifies the missing head height before the architect uses it in design.

handoffSummary.Drawing set: MR-01 room plan and MR-02 sleeve detail

projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side source and finished drawing for mechanical room record drawing set

comparison.label: Before · Contractor field markup
comparison.alt: Mechanical room reference plan with a marked return branch reroute
comparison.caption: M-01 marks a horizontal route change. M-02 records the missing sleeve height.

comparison.label: After · Record plan
comparison.alt: Green return branch around the fixed pump footprint, with a red issue tag near the sleeve
comparison.caption: The revised route stays tied to the source. E-M01 points to the sleeve review.

projects.context: A fictional mechanical contractor supplies a return branch reroute for a turnover set. The plan geometry is available, and the contractor still owes one elevation.
constraints: Keep the P-01 footprint in the supplied location.
Apply the supplied horizontal reroute only.
Carry the sleeve location into the detail and hold its centerline height for field verification.

approach.title: Retain the base
approach.text: Keep the room boundary, equipment footprint and original route for comparison.

approach.title: Incorporate M-01
approach.text: Draw the field-marked route on the record layer and tag the open sleeve on MR-01.

approach.title: Link M-02 to the detail
approach.text: Put the open height on MR-02 and assign the field response in the review register.

deliverables: Editable CAD layouts for the room plan and sleeve detail
Matching record PDF and field markup PDF
Source and exception register
verification: Measure the five-foot horizontal shift against M-01 and check the unchanged P-01 footprint.
Compare MR-01 and MR-02 with the plotted sheets.
Find E-M01 in the drawing set and confirm the reviewer sees the pending centerline height.
projects.review: The contractor provides the verified sleeve elevation and the mechanical reviewer approves the record issue.

handoffSummary.Drawing set: AD-01 plan and AD-02 detail at R1

comparison.label: Before · R0 and bulletin markup
comparison.alt: Original pad outline with the six-foot extension marked in red
comparison.caption: AB-02 extends the east edge by six feet and supplies the change to both sheets.

comparison.label: After · R1 plan
comparison.alt: The 33-foot revised pad appears in green with its previous outline dashed
comparison.caption: AD-01 carries the new width and refers to AD-02. The supplier pattern is still pending.

projects.context: A fictional project team needs to carry a design bulletin through a plan and detail before releasing the next issue. The bulletin includes a pad dimension and identifies an outstanding supplier input.
constraints: Apply only the supplied six-foot eastward extension.
Use the same issue revision and pad width on both sheets.
Keep the anchor pattern open for the design reviewer.

approach.title: Index the bulletin
approach.text: Record A-01 and A-02 against AB-02 in the change register.

approach.title: Synchronize the geometry
approach.text: Update the 27-foot plan outline and detail to 33 feet while preserving the prior outline as a reference.

approach.title: Check the issue set
approach.text: Compare layout IDs, R1 stamps, width labels and the open item in CAD and PDF.

deliverables: Matching R1 plan and detail in one editable CAD file and two PDF sheets
Source markup and an issue register with both dispositions
verification: Measure the 33-foot revised width in both model views.
Confirm AD-01 and AD-02 both show R1 and match the plotted set.
Trace the open anchor pattern to A-02 and confirm who owns the next decision.
projects.review: The supplier confirms the anchor layout. The design lead reviews the information and releases the next issue.

projects.title: Utility road crossing review exhibit
projects.summary: A plan and section bring the supplied crossing route and right-of-way limits into one review set.

handoffSummary.Source: RX-M1 roadway base and crossing markup
handoffSummary.Drawing set: RX-01 crossing plan and RX-02 schematic section
handoffSummary.Open review: Existing utility depth at the crossing

projects.imageAlt: Side-by-side source and finished drawing for utility road crossing review exhibit

comparison.label: Before · Road base and markup
comparison.alt: Two road edges and right-of-way limits with the supplied route marked
comparison.caption: RX-M1 shows the crossing route and roadway references from the prime’s source.

comparison.label: After · Crossing plan
comparison.alt: Revised route and pavement edges with stations 12+05 and 12+65
comparison.caption: RX-01 carries the station references and points to the review section on RX-02.

projects.context: A fictional prime consultant supplies a road crossing alignment and schematic section. The utility owner has yet to confirm the depth of an existing line at the crossing.
constraints: Retain the source roadway and right-of-way geometry.
Use the supplied station references. The 60 feet describes the baseline interval.
Mark the existing utility depth as pending and keep the clearance question with the prime.

approach.title: Separate roadway features
approach.text: Keep pavement edges and right-of-way limits on their own layers.

approach.title: Coordinate plan and section
approach.text: Reference RX-02 from RX-01 and show the supplied route in each view.

approach.title: Record the evidence gap
approach.text: Identify the unverified depth on RX-02 and assign the next action to the prime reviewer.

deliverables: Editable crossing plan and schematic section with named layouts
Matching vector PDF and original synthetic markup
Review register for station references and the depth hold
verification: Check the 60-foot baseline interval between 12+05 and 12+65.
Follow the section reference and compare the plotted route with the supplied geometry.
Check that the depth remains open in the section and the register.
projects.review: The owner or field team verifies the depth. The prime engineer determines clearance and manages the permit submittal.
